issues.reason: The clause carries no status atom and is therefore habitual, not episodic, so "letters" is a non-specific object and the instruction set assigns it the bare kind filler (the "pays tax" / "grows wheat" case); the group witness plus (Theme sk_read_1 sk_letter_1) asserts one determinate batch of letters as the theme of a dispositional event, which the sentence does not state.

The specificity half stands — a bare plural in a non-episodic clause is not a determinate set, so (GroupOf sk_village_1 village) posits a fixed set of source villages the habitual claim does not — but the "each member is neighbouring" half does not: once a group witness exists, distributing a descriptive modifier over its members is exactly what Compound concepts and the plural bar mandate.

gaps_confirmed: a restrictively modified bare-plural object in a generic/habitual clause: the bare kind filler is mandated for the non-specific object, but nothing then carries the "from neighbouring villages" restriction
defect_summary: For the object the compliant filler is the bare kind — (Theme sk_read_1 letter) — but the instruction set then licenses NO form for the restriction: an entity-attached (From letter …) would assert that letters at large come from those villages, and a bare kind leaves "neighbouring" no bearer, so with "carry the restriction or leave the whole claim out and record the gap" as the only fallback the sentence has no fully compliant encoding (the gap above).
notes: "The Council" is correctly a capitalized common noun and a singular collective that does not distribute; entity-attached From for origin, "neighbouring" read as a participial modifier turned adjective, and Manner "aloud" are each right.
